- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.6), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to account for reversal.  
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; if forecast shows >10% spike from prior period, reduce peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period rallies; add 1–2% buffer to final 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., +0.6, -0.6, +0.6), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead in direction of sentiment trend.
